shots.prompt: Morning over the old European city, sunlight on rooftops, but strange: a school of glowing goldfish swims slowly through the air between the chimneys
lines: Four nights left. And the runaway dream was getting bolder.

shots.prompt: Mira at the kitchen table at breakfast notices her cereal milk swirling into tiny stars by itself
Mira finishes breakfast, grabs her school bag and walks to the door, natural movement
Anna in nurse scrubs with a mug of tea, smiling at her daughter
lines: You were sleepwalking again last night. Your shoes were wet.

shots.prompt: Mira at the kitchen table, caught, smiling nervously
lines: Weird dreams, I guess. Can I go early today?

shots.prompt: Mira walks down the sunny street to school; glowing goldfish swim through the air past her, people don't notice
Mira walks down the street to school, looking up in wonder at golden fish swimming in the air
lines: The city was waking up. And so were the dreams.

shots.prompt: Theo waiting at the bus stop, staring up, a goldfish floating next to his face
lines: Mira. There is a fish. In the air. Looking at me.

shots.prompt: Mira on the sunny street, calm, smiling
lines: Don't make eye contact. It's from someone's dream.

shots.prompt: Inside the old school hallway, paper drawings on the walls start moving by themselves, a drawn bird flaps out of a poster
Classroom: the chalkboard writing slowly rearranges itself into a starry night sky; students gasp and laugh
Mira sits in class, glances at the window, then quietly takes out her lantern under the desk
Theo at his desk leaning toward Mira, whispering
lines: Okay, this is getting worse. Like, way worse.

shots.prompt: Mira at her desk, holding the silver bell under the desk, whispering
lines: Elias said daylight makes dreams stranger. It's trying to hide.

shots.prompt: Under the desk the tiny silver bell glows and rings softly
Through the classroom window, a silver ribbon of light flies across the schoolyard toward the old greenhouse
Mira jumps up, determined
Mira and Theo run across the sunny schoolyard toward an old glass greenhouse
Mira and Theo walk side by side through the school yard, talking and laughing
lines: For the first time, Mira wasn't the only one who could see.

shots.prompt: Inside an old glass greenhouse, flowers bloom and close in seconds, petals float upward like snow, golden light
Theo in the greenhouse amazed, petals floating around him
lines: Okay. I take it back. This part is beautiful.

shots.prompt: The silver ribbon of light curls among the floating petals, playful, like a child hiding
Mira kneels slowly in the greenhouse, speaking softly toward the light
lines: You don't have to hide. I just want to know who you belong to.

shots.prompt: The light draws a glowing picture in the misty glass of the greenhouse: a tiny house with a big star above it
Mira stares at the drawing, stunned
lines: That's my house. That's… our star.

shots.prompt: Theo looks at Mira, gentle
lines: Your star? What do you mean?

shots.prompt: Mira, emotional, remembering
lines: When I was little, someone showed me a star from our window. I don't remember who.

shots.prompt: Outside the greenhouse glass, a tall shadow in a wide-brimmed hat walks past slowly, the flowers near the glass wilt and close
Theo freezes, whispering
The silver light dives into Mira's brass lantern and hides inside, the flame glowing silver
The greenhouse door creaks open slowly, cold mist spills in, but only an empty doorway with falling petals
Mira holds the lantern close to her chest, whispering
lines: It's okay. I've got you. I promise.

shots.prompt: Evening, the school empty, the lantern glowing silver in Mira's bag as she walks home with Theo
Mira and Theo walk home together in the evening light, Theo gesturing excitedly
Theo walking home at dusk, serious for once
lines: Mira… if it's your dream, why don't you remember it?

shots.prompt: Mira at dusk on the street, looking up at the first star
lines: I don't know. But tonight, I'm going to find out.

shots.prompt: Night: from Mira's bedroom window a single bright star shines over the rooftops, the lantern glows silver on the sill
lines: Three nights left. And the dream had finally chosen to trust her.
